entry.title: The Exit Criteria Pattern: Know When to Stop Iterating with AI
entry.summary:
Here's a pattern I see constantly: a developer asks AI to refactor a function, gets a decent result, then spends 45 minutes on follow-up prompts trying to make it "perfect." The final version is barely better than the third iteration — and sometimes worse. The problem isn't the AI. It's that you never defined what "done" looks like. Before you start any AI-assisted task, write exit criteria. Literally. In your prompt. Task: Refactor the processOrder function to handle partial failures.
Exit criteria (stop when ALL are true): - [ ] Each payment/inventory/notification step can fail independently - [ ] Failed steps are logged with enough context to retry manually - [ ] The function returns a result object showing which steps succeeded/failed - [ ] No step takes longer than 5 seconds (timeout…

entry.title: Claude Code custom slash commands: build your own /deploy, /review, /test
entry.summary:
Claude Code custom slash commands: build your own /deploy, /review, /test
Claude Code ships with built-in slash commands like /help, /clear, and /compact. But the real power is in custom commands — project-specific shortcuts that run multi-step workflows with a single word. Here's exactly how to build them. Custom slash commands are Markdown files in a .claude/commands/ directory. When you type /deploy in Claude Code, it reads .claude/commands/deploy.md and executes whatever's in it as a prompt. That's it. No plugins, no config syntax — just Markdown files. your-project/ ├── .claude/ │ └── commands/ │ ├── deploy.md │ ├── review.md │ ├── test.md │ └── standup.md └── src/

The Search Layer The tool generates precision search queries and scans: Reddit (5M+ posts analyzed) Twitter/X (real-time signals) Hacker News (technical insights) Indie Hackers (founder pain points) The Scoring Algorithm Every idea gets a Build Worthiness Score (0-10) based on: Urgency: How desperate is the language? ("nightmare" vs "would be nice") Buying Intent: Are they already paying for inferior solutions? Frequency: How often does this come up? Specificity: Vague complaints score lower than detailed pain descriptions The Customer Finder This is the goldmine. The tool identifies specific people who: Posted "looking for [solution]" in the last 30 days Mentioned budget constraints or willingness to pay Are actively comparing alternatives Frontend: React + Tailwind (deployed on Cloudflare Pages) Backend: Node.js + Express Search: Custom scrapers + Reddit API + Twitter API NLP: OpenAI API for intent classification and urgency scoring Database: PostgreSQL for conversation storage Queue: Redis for handling 10M+ posts efficiently [problem] is frustrating looking for alternative to [solution] [solution] is too expensive how do you handle [problem] Direct quotes (copy/paste) Upvote counts Dates (must be recent) Any mention of budget check out BuildForWho
